whyItLooksGood: Each kick gets a stack of 3-4 arcs at different radii and tilts, which reads as a 3D sweep from any camera instead of a flat ribbon
The arcs double in size in a single frame at the end of the swing: the scale jump is the impact of the swing itself
Hits alternate shapes (a long rainbow-edged streak, then a one-frame spike burst), so a combo never repeats the same sprite
0.15-0.3 s rest beats with no VFX separate the hits so each one reads on its own
buildNotes: Video 0:01.4-0:04.8. Per kick: 3-4 CrescentArc instances (soft dialect, white edge, cyan body) parented to the attacker with yaw following the leg, radii 1.0-1.6 m and tilt offsets of 10-20 degrees; tween scale 1 -> 2 in one frame at the end of the swing, then translate 1 m up-back and fade to grey over 0.15 s. Hit 1: a thin beam-ribbon quad (5 m) along the kick direction with a chromatic shader (offset R and B copies 2-3 px apart) fading over 0.2 s. Hit 2: StarBurst (hard spikes) for 1 frame, Emitter of 10 velocity-stretched needles in a flat fan (drag 4), createRing on the floor with spin, then a SmokeBall dust ring in grey. Leave 0.15-0.3 s of nothing between hits.

buildNotes: Video 0:08.6-0:11.3. Hold the camera on the caster 1.2 s (no effects). ScreenFx: full-screen dark navy (#0a0f1c) with a camera-facing quad (black fill, white rim shader), tween rotation 90->10 deg and width 30%->0.2% over 0.25 s with ease-in. Then 1 white frame, 2 frames inverted skeleton card (NEW silhouette card, outline mode), 2 frames black card with a white wedge polygon. Back in world: a thin white line quad across the target at the same angle, a decal line on the dummy, a slow fleck Emitter. Medium shake only on the return to 3D.
